takeaways: Modern Microsoft 365 breaches bypass MFA by combining consent phishing with adversary-in-the-middle token theft rather than breaking passwords.
OAuth app consent and refresh tokens survive password resets, so remediation must revoke grants, remove service principals, invalidate tokens and remove malicious inbox rules.

Disabling user consent, enforcing the admin consent workflow, turning on token protection and risk-based Conditional Access, plus Sentinel playbooks on consent, forwarding and download events break the chain.
hook: Think MFA keeps attackers out of your Microsoft 365 tenant? This episode maps a real breach chain from consent phishing and token theft to OAuth persistence and SharePoint exfiltration for security teams and admins. You get the exact logs, Sentinel detections and Entra policies that stop it.
